Episode 41 of @RuntimeArguments is live at RuntimeArguments.fm: "Efficiency at Any Scale, with Marlon Dutra". Our first-ever guest! Longtime friend Marlon Dutra of Meta, whom Jim @jammcq met on IRC back in the LTSP days, leads a practical tour of software efficiency, and his case is that it isn't just for huge systems: your code may run on a five-year-old phone, in a car for decades, or up a cloud bill. Efficiency also isn't performance. Make something 20% slower and 10x cheaper, and if nobody notices, that's a win. Measure first (even a text file beats no data), then CPU (big O, hot paths, profilers, CPU time vs. wall time), memory (by Marlon's rough count, about 75% of the cost of a server rack, plus cache lines and locality), I/O (N+1 queries, Parquet, SSD wear) and networking (batch your round trips, and back off exponentially so your retries don't take down your own servers). Wolf @YesJustWolf brings a story of profiling an accidentally quadratic docs build that dropped from 20 minutes to 24 seconds. Marlon's five-line code examples are on our GitHub: https://github.com/Runtime-Arguments/efficiency. Also: the show has passed 5,000 downloads. Thank you for listening!
